questions.stem: « Piscine municipale : fermée pour travaux du 3 au 17 août. Réouverture le 18 août à 9 h. » Why is the pool closed?
options: For building work
For a swimming competition
For a public holiday
Because of a staff shortage
questions.explanation: « Fermée pour travaux » means closed for works, such as repairs or building. The dates give the length of the closure, not a holiday.

questions.stem: « Interdit de stationner sauf livraisons. » Who may park here?
options: Residents only
Anyone, for a short time
Nobody, at any time
Delivery vehicles only
questions.explanation: « Sauf » means 'except', so parking is banned for everyone except deliveries. Missing the « sauf » leads to 'nobody, at any time'.

questions.stem: « Offre spéciale : deux places achetées, la troisième offerte ! » What is the offer?
options: A third ticket at half price
Two tickets for the price of three
Three tickets for the price of one
Buy two tickets, get a third free
questions.explanation: « Offert » means given as a gift, so the third ticket costs nothing. The word looks like 'offered', but in shops and ads it means 'free'.

questions.stem: « Ouvert du lundi au samedi. Fermé le dimanche et les jours fériés. » When is the shop closed?
options: On public holidays only
On Sundays and public holidays
On Mondays and public holidays
On Saturdays and Sundays
questions.explanation: « Les jours fériés » are public holidays, and the shop is also closed on Sundays. « Du lundi au samedi » means it is open from Monday to Saturday.

questions.stem: « Musée ouvert tous les jours sauf le mardi, de 9 h à 18 h. Nocturne le jeudi jusqu'à 21 h 45. » When can you visit at 8 pm?
options: On no day of the week
On Thursday
On Tuesday
On any day of the week
questions.explanation: « Une nocturne » is a late opening, here until 9.45 pm on Thursdays. On other days the museum closes at 6 pm, and on Tuesdays it does not open at all.

questions.stem: « Cherche étudiant(e) pour garder deux enfants le mercredi après-midi. Expérience exigée. Bonne rémunération. » What does the job require?
options: Previous experience
A driving licence
Fluent English
Weekend availability
questions.explanation: « Exigé » means 'required', so experience is essential. The job is on Wednesday afternoons, not weekends, and « bonne rémunération » means it pays well.

questions.stem: « Inscriptions au séjour linguistique avant le 15 avril. Places limitées. Tarif réduit pour les frères et sœurs. » Who gets a discount?
options: Students under the age of 15
Groups of fifteen or more
Siblings enrolling together
Anyone who enrols early
questions.explanation: « Tarif réduit pour les frères et sœurs » gives the discount to siblings. The 15 April date is a deadline for enrolling, not a discount.

questions.stem: « Dsl, je suis en retard, le bus est en panne. J'arrive dans 10 min. Bises, Chloé » Why is Chloé late?
options: She is stuck in traffic.
She overslept.
Her bus has broken down.
She missed her bus.
questions.explanation: « En panne » means broken down. « Dsl » is text-message shorthand for « désolée », 'sorry'.

questions.stem: « Chère Madame Martin, je vous écris pour vous remercier de votre accueil chaleureux pendant mon séjour à Lyon. » What is the purpose of the email?
options: To thank her for her hospitality
To ask to stay with her again
To complain about the stay
To book a room in Lyon
questions.explanation: « Vous remercier de votre accueil chaleureux » is thanking her for a warm welcome. « Je vous écris pour… » is a standard way to state a letter's purpose at the start.

questions.stem: « Salut ! Ça roule ? Trop hâte de te voir ce week-end ! » Who is this most likely written to?
options: A close friend
A future employer
A school principal
A host family not yet met
questions.explanation: « Salut », « ça roule ? » and « tu » are all informal, and « trop hâte » is casual teenage speech. Every other reader would need « vous » and a formal opening.

questions.stem: « Dans l'attente de votre réponse, je vous prie d'agréer, Monsieur, mes salutations distinguées. » Where would this sentence appear?
options: On a sign in a shop
At the end of a formal letter
At the start of a text to a friend
In a newspaper headline
questions.explanation: This is a set closing formula for formal letters, with « vous » and « salutations distinguées ». It is far too formal for a text to a friend.

questions.stem: « Salut Tom, je ne pourrai pas venir à ta fête samedi, désolé. Par contre, on se voit lundi au lycée ? » What does the writer suggest?
options: Meeting at school on Monday instead
Moving the party to Monday
Coming to the party late on Saturday
Seeing Tom at the party on Saturday
questions.explanation: « Par contre » ('on the other hand') introduces an alternative: seeing each other at school on Monday. The party itself is not moved, and the writer cannot come on Saturday.

questions.stem: « Depuis que j'ai supprimé Instagram, je dors mieux et je lis davantage. Bien sûr, mes amis me manquent un peu. » What has changed for the writer?
options: She spends more time online.
She sleeps better and reads more.
She has lost touch with all her friends.
She reads less but sleeps longer.
questions.explanation: « Davantage » means 'more', and « je dors mieux » is 'I sleep better'. She misses her friends « un peu », which is far from losing them all.

questions.stem: « Certes, le télétravail fait gagner du temps. Pourtant, beaucoup de salariés se sentent isolés loin de leurs collègues. » What is the writer's view?
options: Staff like working from home because they prefer to be alone.
Working from home brings staff closer to their colleagues.
Working from home saves time but can isolate staff.
Working from home wastes time and isolates staff.
questions.explanation: « Certes … pourtant » concedes a point and then raises a drawback. Time is saved, but many feel isolated. The writer does not say time is wasted.

questions.stem: « Le scénario est prévisible, mais les acteurs sont tellement convaincants qu'on ne s'ennuie jamais. » What is the reviewer's overall opinion?
options: The plot is surprising but the acting is weak.
Both the plot and the acting are disappointing.
The acting makes up for a predictable plot.
The film is boring because the plot is predictable.
questions.explanation: « Prévisible » is a criticism, but « tellement convaincants qu'on ne s'ennuie jamais » is strong praise. Because of the acting, you are never bored.

questions.stem: « Même si la vie à Paris coûte cher, je ne la quitterais pour rien au monde. » What does the writer say?
options: She would leave Paris because it is too expensive.
Life in Paris is cheaper than people think.
She is planning to leave Paris before long.
Paris is expensive, but she would never leave it.
questions.explanation: « Même si » ('even if') concedes the cost, and « pour rien au monde » means 'not for anything in the world'. The conditional « quitterais » refers to a hypothetical departure, not a plan.

questions.stem: « Ce qui m'a le plus frappé à Québec, ce sont les vieilles rues en pierre du quartier historique. » What impressed the writer most?
options: The cold winters of the city
The food served in the old quarter
The French spoken in the streets
The old stone streets
questions.explanation: « Ce qui m'a le plus frappé, ce sont… » means 'what struck me most was…'. Here « frapper » means 'to strike' or 'impress', not 'to hit'.

questions.stem: « Ce n'est pas que je n'aime pas le sport, c'est que je n'ai pas le temps. » What is the speaker's point?
options: She likes sport but has no time for it.
She dislikes sport and has no time for it.
She has the time but no interest in sport.
She makes time for sport every day.
questions.explanation: « Ce n'est pas que… c'est que… » rejects one explanation and gives the real one. The double negative « pas que je n'aime pas » means she does like sport.

questions.stem: « Encore une grève ! Bravo, vraiment, pour ceux qui doivent aller travailler… » What is the writer's tone?
options: Grateful
Neutral
Enthusiastic
Sarcastic
questions.explanation: « Encore une » shows exasperation, and « bravo, vraiment » means the opposite of what it says. The trailing dots invite the reader to share the irony.

questions.stem: « Le festival accueillera plus de 200 artistes venus de 30 pays francophones, du 5 au 9 juillet à Montréal. » What is the general subject?
options: An international francophone arts festival
A music school for young francophone artists
A trade fair for French-speaking businesses
A summer sports camp held in Montréal
questions.explanation: The general meaning is a festival of artists from many French-speaking countries. The numbers, dates and city are specific details that support it.

questions.stem: « Le maire avait promis de nouvelles pistes cyclables. Deux ans plus tard, les habitants attendent toujours. » What does the writer imply?
options: The mayor has just cancelled the bike paths.
The promised bike paths have not been built.
The new bike paths were finished two years ago.
Residents voted against building bike paths.
questions.explanation: « Attendre toujours » means 'still to be waiting', so the promise has not been kept. Nothing says the project was cancelled; the criticism is left implied.

questions.stem: « Grâce au tri sélectif, la commune a réduit ses déchets de 20 % en deux ans. » What does the text report?
options: The town's waste rose by 20% over two years.
The town plans to cut its waste by 20% within two years.
Only 20% of the town's waste is recycled.
Recycling helped the town cut its waste by 20% in two years.
questions.explanation: « Grâce à » credits a cause, « a réduit » is a completed result, and « de 20 % » gives the size of the cut. It is not a plan, because the verb is in the passé composé.

questions.stem: « Faute de moyens, l'association a dû fermer ses portes. » Why did the organisation close?
options: Someone made a serious mistake.
It had too many members.
It moved to a new building.
It ran out of money.
questions.explanation: « Faute de » means 'for lack of', and « les moyens » are the means, usually money. Reading « faute » as 'fault' or 'mistake' is the trap.

questions.stem: « Les jeunes Français sont de plus en plus nombreux à partir étudier à l'étranger. » What trend does the sentence describe?
options: More and more young French people study abroad.
Fewer young French people now study abroad.
Most foreign students choose to study in France.
Young French people prefer to study at home.
questions.explanation: « De plus en plus nombreux » means 'more and more numerous', and « à l'étranger » means 'abroad'. The sentence is about French students leaving France, not foreign students arriving.

questions.stem: « Il ne s'agit pas d'interdire les portables, mais d'apprendre à s'en servir avec modération. » What is the writer's position?
options: Phones should be used in moderation, not banned.
Phones should be banned until people learn to use them.
Phones are harmless, so there is nothing to learn.
Only adults should be allowed to use phones.
questions.explanation: « Il ne s'agit pas de… mais de… » means 'it's not about…, but about…': the writer rejects a ban. « S'en servir » is 'to use them', with « en » standing for the phones.

questions.stem: « A : Le train est plus écologique que l'avion. B : Pourtant, le billet de train coûte souvent plus cher. » How does B respond to A?
options: B changes the subject to something unrelated.
B raises a drawback without denying A's point.
B agrees with A and adds another benefit.
B shows that A's claim is false.
questions.explanation: « Pourtant » ('and yet') sets a drawback, the cost, against A's point about the environment. B never says the train is less ecological, so A's claim stands.

questions.stem: « J'ai acheté des cerises au marché, mais j'en ai déjà mangé la moitié ! » What does « en » refer to?
options: The fruit stall at the market
The money
The morning
The cherries
questions.explanation: « En » replaces « de » + a noun, here « des cerises »: 'I have already eaten half of them'. A place such as the market would be « y ».

questions.stem: « Ma correspondante m'a envoyé un colis. Je l'ai ouvert tout de suite. » What does « l' » refer to, and how can you tell?
options: The pen friend, because « l' » here is feminine
The parcel, because « l' » is always masculine
The pen friend, because she is the last person named
The parcel, because « ouvert » has no feminine -e
questions.explanation: « L' » could be « le » or « la ». A preceding direct object makes the participle agree, so « ouvert » with no -e shows the object is masculine: « le colis ». For the pen friend it would be « ouverte ».

questions.stem: « Il était une fois, dans un petit village de Provence, un boulanger qui ne savait pas faire de pain. » What kind of text does this begin?
options: A recipe
A formal letter
A children's story
A news report
questions.explanation: « Il était une fois » is the traditional opening of a story, like 'once upon a time'. The imperfect sets the scene, as it does at the start of most narratives.

questions.stem: « Après la rentrée, toute la famille reprend le rythme métro-boulot-dodo. » What does « métro-boulot-dodo » describe?
options: A new public transport timetable for the city
A bedtime routine for very young children
The daily grind of commuting, work and sleep
A relaxing holiday routine by the sea
questions.explanation: The phrase strings together the metro, « le boulot » (work) and « dodo » (a child's word for sleep). It sums up a repetitive working routine and has no exact English equivalent.

questions.stem: « Léa a eu son bac avec mention très bien. Ses parents ont sabré le champagne. » How did her parents react?
options: They celebrated.
They were disappointed.
They were worried.
They were angry.
questions.explanation: « Sabrer le champagne » is to open champagne to celebrate. « Mention très bien » is one of the top results in the bac, so there is plenty to celebrate.

questions.stem: « Il pleuvait des cordes, alors nous avons annulé le pique-nique. » Why was the picnic cancelled?
options: It was pouring with rain.
The ropes had broken.
It was far too hot.
Nobody turned up.
questions.explanation: « Pleuvoir des cordes » ('to rain ropes') is an idiom for heavy rain, like 'raining cats and dogs'. Taking « cordes » literally gives the rope answer.

questions.stem: « Je me suis inscrite au club de théâtre, histoire de rencontrer du monde. » Why did the writer join the club?
options: To become famous
To meet people
To study history
To see the world
questions.explanation: Informal « histoire de » + infinitive means 'just to' or 'so as to', and « rencontrer du monde » means meeting people. Neither « histoire » nor « monde » carries its usual meaning here.

questions.stem: « Mon frère aîné, qui fait des études de médecine, rentre à la maison un week-end sur deux. » How often does he come home?
options: Two weekends a year
Every second weekend
Every weekend
Twice every weekend
questions.explanation: « Un week-end sur deux » is 'one weekend in two'. « Aîné » means 'older', and « faire des études de médecine » is studying medicine.

questions.stem: « Je suis fils unique, mais mes cousins sont comme des frères pour moi. » What do we learn about the writer?
options: He has one brother.
His cousins are his brothers.
He doesn't get on with his cousins.
He has no brothers or sisters.
questions.explanation: « Fils unique » means an only child (a son). His cousins are only « comme des frères », 'like brothers'.

questions.stem: « Pour réussir sa pâte à crêpes, il faut la laisser reposer une heure avant la cuisson. » What is the advice?
options: Rest for an hour after eating crêpes.
Make the batter an hour after cooking.
Let the batter rest for an hour before cooking.
Cook the crêpes for a full hour.
questions.explanation: « La » refers to « la pâte », the batter, and « reposer » means 'to rest'. « Avant la cuisson » means 'before cooking'.

questions.stem: « Le conférencier a fait une intervention passionnante sur l'avenir de l'énergie. » What did the speaker do?
options: He broke up a fight.
He rudely interrupted.
He gave a fascinating talk.
He performed an operation.
questions.explanation: In this context « une intervention » is a talk or contribution, and « passionnant » means 'fascinating'. The English 'intervention' suggests stepping in, which is the false friend.

questions.stem: « À la fin du stage, chaque participant recevra une attestation. » What will each participant receive?
options: An offer of a job
A certificate of attendance
A payment for their work
A uniform for the course
questions.explanation: « Une attestation » is an official document confirming something, here completion of a course. « Un stage » here is a training course or placement.

questions.stem: « Avant de quitter la salle, veuillez éteindre les lumières et fermer les fenêtres. » What are you asked to do?
options: Leave the lights on and close the windows
Turn off the lights and open the windows
Turn off the lights and close the windows
Turn on the lights and open the windows
questions.explanation: « Éteindre » is 'to switch off' and « fermer » is 'to close'. « Veuillez » + infinitive is the polite formula for written instructions.

questions.stem: « Le gouvernement a annoncé que les transports seraient gratuits pour les moins de 18 ans dès la rentrée. » What was announced?
options: Free transport for under-18s from the new school year
Free transport for over-18s starting next year
Cheaper transport for students already at university
A plan to study free transport for young people
questions.explanation: « Gratuit » means 'free', « les moins de 18 ans » are under-18s, and « dès la rentrée » is 'from the start of the school year'. The conditional « seraient » reports what was announced, not a mere study.
